reader.requirement: Several REDEFINES entries may redefine the same character positions, and each must name as data-name-2 the entry that originally defined the area; a REDEFINES naming an entry that is itself a redefinition must be refused, at subordinate levels and at 01/77.

edition-consulted.switches: COBOL1656 is an error under strict and a warning under --permissive (chain accepted); not keyed on the edition

reader.edition-search: Grepped ResolveRedefinesPass.cs, ClassifyRedefinesClassesPass.cs and DataItem.RedefinedEntry for Edition.Edition, .Year, CobolVersion, Constructs., ConstructRegistry: none. The only edition-adjacent consult is EditionContext.Removed, the strict/permissive severity seam.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f09_01 covers the acceptance (RD1, RD2 both REDEFINES ORIG). The refusal of a chain is not exercised.

probes.expected: accepted: B (numeric), C (group), D (shorter) all REDEFINES A; 77 W2 and W3 both REDEFINES W1; all share A's / W1's positions

probes.printed: error COBOL1656: 'C' REDEFINES 'B', which is itself a redefinition - data-name-2 shall be the entry that originally defined the storage area (ISO §2023:13.18.44.3 SR7)
error COBOL1656: 'R3' REDEFINES 'R2', which is itself a redefinition

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.5.10.3 SR8  (5.10.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR8

reader.notes: Multiple redefinitions bind and share storage; a chain is refused with COBOL1656 under strict. Under --permissive the chain is a warning and binds to the anchor, a documented leniency outside the strict conformance mode.

refuter.evidence: Attacked the chain refusal inside a nested (level-2, SR12) redefinition: 10 B3 REDEFINES B2 where B2 REDEFINES B1 under 05 B REDEFINES A (d4nest) refused COBOL1656 at --std 85; multiple redefinitions of B1 and of A in the same program (d5nestok) accepted. Default mode is strict (error); the --permissive warning is EditionContext.Removed, not edition-keyed. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.5.10.3 SR8  (5.10.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR8'.
